symptom: Under `mdl 1;` re-running an edited `describe` of a microflow/nanoflow through `create or modify` was refused whenever the edit touched the header or a document property (URL, export level, concurrency, documentation, return type, parameters) — doctype-tests/microflow-document-properties failed at Deeplink.ACT_Import — or moved a node with a new @position/@start (bug-tests/951); under mdl 0 the same edits fell back to the lossy whole-flow rebuild (MDL-V1-REBUILD). And the splice silently ignored a stated @position on an inserted statement, placing it itself (both versions, alter microflow too).
cause: diff-then-patch compared the header as a whole and refused any difference, since the splice engine (mfmutator) could only insert/replace/drop activities; the statement match (declaredMatches) treated a stated position different from the stored one as a different statement, which fell into a gap and was refused as 'moved'; and spliceOnFlow/Replace always translated a fragment into the gap, dropping the builder's placement.
file: mdl/backend/mfmutator/header.go (SetHeader, setParameters); mdl/backend/mfmutator/splice.go (Move, MicroflowFragment.Placed); mdl/executor/cmd_flow_modify.go, cmd_flow_modify_patch.go (weighted LCS, moved/startEvent/followingEnd, parameterMoves, checkRemovedParameters); mdl/executor/flow_declared_match.go (matchAnyPosition)
insight: A header is not part of the graph: every header property is a value of the unit (or a parameter object no flow touches), so it is patchable by encoding the declared document exactly as the rebuild would and copying only the whitelisted header keys whose canonical value differs (CarryTranslations + TransplantIDs confined to that value, so an unchanged property is not rewritten and a text keeps its other languages). Watch storage names: Mendix stores ConcurrencyErrorMessage as `ConcurrenyErrorMessage` and a parameter's type as `VariableType` — both made a first cut silently report 'Unchanged'. A move is a position only (flows keep sides and control vectors); match moved statements in the LCS with a lower weight than exact ones so an alike stored statement left in place keeps its node. Apply moves before AND after the splice ops (a placed fragment next to a moved node is joined where it now is; a shift cannot undo a stated position). Because mdl 0 takes the same patch path, the upgrade property test's equality for these scripts holds by construction — the proof is on Studio Pro-authored flows: strict BSON diff (IDs included, lists matched by $ID) equals exactly the edited values, with an unedited-describe control.
